Rationale: Represents an aggregate contribution of SUCNR1-associated signaling to inflammatory activity. The biological pathway is supported by Macias-Ceja et al. (2019), but this specific feedback coefficient has not been experimentally measured.

Represents the aggregate inflammatory contribution of CD150+ monocyte activity. Ke et al. (2024) identified inflammatory mediators associated with these cells, but did not directly estimate this ODE feedback coefficient.

Represents first-order relaxation of normalized inflammatory activity. The selected value gives a mathematical half-life of approximately 1.39 days. This is an exploratory model timescale, not a measured clinical half-life.

Represents effective succinate production associated with inflammatory activity. The biological relevance of succinate is supported by Macias-Ceja et al. (2019), but this normalized production rate is assumed.

Represents effective first-order removal of extracellular succinate. The baseline implies a mathematical half-life of approximately 0.69 days. No direct intestinal clearance time-course has been used to estimate this value.

Represents the maximum normalized activation input of the succinate-SUCNR1 signaling state. The pathway is supported by Macias-Ceja et al. (2019), but this maximum activation rate has not been fitted.

Succinate is normalized using a reference concentration of 1 mM. Macias-Ceja et al. (2019) tested several succinate concentrations, including 0.1, 0.5, 1, and 5 mM. The selected value is an exploratory saturation scale within this range. It is not an experimentally fitted EC50.
Evidence: Experimental dose range informs exploration; K assumed

Rationale: Represents effective first-order relaxation of normalized SUCNR1 signaling. The value implies a mathematical half-life of approximately 0.99 days. It is not a measured receptor turnover rate.
Represents the maximum normalized activation input to the monocyte activity state. The involvement of CD150+ inflammatory monocytes is supported by Ke et al. (2024), but this rate is assumed.
Controls saturation of monocyte activation in response to normalized inflammatory activity. A matching quantitative dose-response experiment has not yet been used to estimate this parameter.
Represents effective relaxation of normalized monocyte activity. It must not be interpreted as the physical lifespan or clearance rate of CD150+ monocytes.
Represents maximum normalized TWIST1 activation associated with monocyte-derived profibrotic signals. Ke et al. (2024) demonstrated TWIST1-associated responses, but this ODE rate is assumed.
Controls saturation of TWIST1 activation in response to normalized monocyte activity. A quantitative dose-response curve suitable for estimating this value has not yet been extracted.
Represents effective relaxation of TWIST1-related activity. Experimental stimulation duration must not be interpreted as a TWIST1 decay half-life.

Represents the maximum normalized fibroblast activation input associated with SUCNR1 signaling. Macias-Ceja et al. (2019) supports succinate-related fibroblast responses, but the numerical rate has not yet been fitted.
Controls saturation of the fibroblast response to SUCNR1 signaling. This is a model response constant and is not equivalent to the ligand EC50 of SUCNR1.
Represents maximum normalized fibroblast activation associated with TWIST1. Ke et al. (2024) supports TWIST1-dependent fibroblast activation and ECM production, but this rate is assumed.
Controls saturation of fibroblast activation in response to TWIST1 activity. No matching quantitative dose-response curve has yet been used to estimate this parameter.
Represents effective relaxation of normalized profibrotic fibroblast activity. It is not the lifespan of fibroblasts and is not directly measured in the cited study.
Represents ECM production per unit normalized fibroblast activity. Increased collagen deposition is supported by Ke et al. (2024), but this normalized production coefficient is assumed.
Represents effective first-order ECM removal. The baseline implies a mathematical half-life of approximately 27.73 days. It is not a measured collagen half-life in Crohn's disease tissue.

Represents a proposed recruitment input from fibroblast activity to monocyte activity. Ke et al. (2024) supports potential chemokine-mediated communication, but this ODE recruitment coefficient has not been measured.
Controls saturation of the proposed fibroblast-associated recruitment response. No matching quantitative recruitment dose-response curve has yet been used to estimate this parameter.
